findings.title: Custom ClassLoader defineClass()+newInstance() of local .class files, auto-triggered from mario.properties at startup
findings.code_excerpt: byte data[] = loadClassData(filename); ... c = defineClass(data, 0, data.length);  // then in getAI(): o = c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: (a) 'aiLeft'/'aiRight' values in mario.properties in the current working directory, read unattended at startup; (b) any .class file picked in the 'load player' JFileChooser (menu/analysis frame)
findings.sink: ClassLoader.defineClass (ApoMarioClassLoader.java:74) followed by Class.newInstance (:41); loaded object's think() then runs every game tick
findings.data_path: ApoMarioConstants.loadProperties() reads mario.properties via new FileInputStream("mario.properties") (ApoMarioConstants.java:39,90) -> AI_LEFT/AI_RIGHT (:129-130) -> ApoMarioPanel.loadPropertiesPlayer passes the non-numeric string to loadPlayer (ApoMarioPanel.java:153-154,176) -> ApoMarioLevel.loadPlayer(int,String) splits path/classname (ApoMarioLevel.java:1023-1048) -> loadPlayer(player,path,classname,classN) calls new ApoMarioClassLoader(path,classname).getAI() (ApoMarioLevel.java:1074) -> loadClassData() reads raw bytes from disk (ApoMarioClassLoader.java:106-129)
findings.attack_scenario: Variant 1 (persistence, no interaction): attacker distributes a zip 'level pack' containing evil/Evil.class (extends ApoMarioAI, constructor writes files/starts connections) plus a mario.properties with aiLeft=C:\...\evil\Evil.class. Victim extracts next to the jar and launches ApoMarioMain; during init() the class is defined and instantiated before any click. Variant 2 (competition plugin model): victim downloads another player's 'AI' .class and loads it via the menu; it runs with full JVM privileges - no SecurityManager exists anywhere in the tree.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode (B_APPLET==false; guard at ApoMarioLevel.java:1073). For the properties vector: write access to the directory the game is started from, and a Windows-style backslash path (loadPlayer uses File.separator-'\\' parsing at ApoMarioLevel.java:1044-1046); on Linux/macOS the default parsing yields empty source dir, though crafted dotted values still resolve relative to CWD. For the chooser vector: user consent to load the file.
findings.validation_plan: Compile Evil.java extends apoMario.ai.ApoMarioAI whose constructor writes C:/pwned.txt. Place it beside the jar, add mario.properties containing aiLeft=C\:\\path\\Evil.class, run java -jar ApoMario.jar. pwned.txt appears with zero interaction; ApoMarioConstants.saveProperties() (called at ApoMarioLevel.java:1092 and window close) re-persists the path, making it sticky. Repeat via Menu > Load Player picking Evil.class.

findings.title: Unvalidated width/height integers from hand-parsed .mar level file drive giant array allocation (OOM crash)
findings.code_excerpt: int width = data.readInt(); int height = data.readInt(); ... this.level.setLevelEntities(new ApoMarioEntity[height][width]);
findings.entry_point: A malicious .mar editor-level file opened via 'Load level' file chooser (ApoMarioPanel.loadEditorLevel, ApoMarioPanel.java:251-256), or referenced indirectly by a crafted .rep replay (see ApoMario-04)
findings.sink: new ApoMarioEntity[height][width] allocation and the subsequent width*height readInt() parse loop (ApoMarioEditorIO.java:59-96)
findings.data_path: JFileChooser path -> editorIO.readLevel(path) (ApoMarioPanel.java:255) -> ApoMarioEditorIO.readLevel(DataInputStream) reads first two ints as dimensions with no bounds check (lines 53-54) -> array allocation (line 57). OutOfMemoryError is an Error, so the catch(Exception ex) at line 129 does NOT catch it and the EDT/thread dies
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker shares a '.mar level' whose first 8 bytes encode width=height=0x7FFFFFF0. Victim loads it in the editor; the JVM attempts a ~2^60-element reference array, throws OutOfMemoryError, and the game dies (or hangs thrashing GC with moderately large values like 20000x20000 while allocating per-tile BufferedImages in makeWall/makeGroundWall).
findings.preconditions: User opens the hostile .mar file; negative dimensions instead throw NegativeArraySizeException which IS swallowed by catch(Exception) at line 129 (harmless).
findings.validation_plan: Create mar.bin with DataOutputStream.writeInt(Integer.MAX_VALUE-15) twice plus a few trailing ints; rename to evil.mar; Editor > Load level; observe immediate OutOfMemoryError on console / process death. Compare with width=100,height=15 control file which loads normally.

findings.title: Replay-header width/difficulty reused unvalidated to size level arrays and scale enemy-generation loops
findings.code_excerpt: this.width = Integer.valueOf(reader.readLine()); this.difficulty = Integer.valueOf(reader.readLine()); this.random = Long.valueOf(reader.readLine());
findings.entry_point: A crafted .rep replay file opened via Menu > Load Replay (ApoMarioMenu.java:453-455 / ApoMarioAnalysis.java:293-296 -> ApoMarioPanel.loadReplay, ApoMarioPanel.java:274-283)
findings.sink: ApoMarioReplayPlay.initReplay() feeds replay.getWidth()/getDifficulty() into level.makeLevel (ApoMarioReplayPlay.java:52-54) -> this.width=width then new ApoMarioEntity[this.height][this.width] (ApoMarioLevel.java:331-337), plus difficulty-scaled generation loops in ApoMarioRandomLevel.makeRandomLevel (uncapped enemies count: random.nextInt((int)(1+difficulty/45f)) at ApoMarioRandomLevel.java:161)
findings.data_path: replay.load(fileName) -> loadLevel(BufferedReader) parses three header lines with no range checks (ApoMarioReplay.java:305-313) -> setReplay/playReplay(true) (ApoMarioPanel.java:281-291) -> levelRestart(bReplay) -> replayPlay.initReplay() (ApoMarioLevel.java:1112-1113) -> makeLevel(...) allocation and generation. NumberFormatException from garbage lines propagates uncaught (load() catches only IOException, ApoMarioReplay.java:293-303) and kills the calling thread.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker posts a 'world record' .rep with width=2000000000. On load, makeLevel attempts a 15x2e9 entity array -> OutOfMemoryError, game crashes; with width=100000 the game instead freezes for minutes building tiles/enemies. Same file also poisons the level-name line consumed by ApoMario-04.
findings.preconditions: Victim opens the hostile .rep; desktop mode (loadReplay is !B_APPLET-gated).
findings.validation_plan: Write evil.rep with lines: '2000000000','50','-1', then filler name/author/steps lines; Menu > Load Replay; observe OOM. Second file with '5000','700000','-1',... demonstrates multi-minute hang in level generation (sample with jstack showing ApoMarioRandomLevel.makeRandomLevel frames).

findings.title: Path built from replay-controlled levelString allows reading arbitrary files outside levels/ directory
findings.entry_point: levelString line inside a .rep replay file (only present when the replay's random header equals -1), parsed at ApoMarioReplay.java:309-310
findings.data_path: ApoMarioPanel.loadReplay() -> getReplay().load(path) sets levelString from file line 4 (ApoMarioReplay.java:310) -> concatenation at ApoMarioPanel.java:279 -> ApoMarioEditorIO.readLevel(String) -> super.readLevel(fileName) -> ApoIO.readLevel(ApoConstants.B_APPLET,...) -> new FileInputStream(fileName)
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker sends a .rep whose random line is '-1' and levelString line is '..\\..\\..\\Users\\victim\\secret.doc'. When the victim plays the replay, the game opens that file and interprets its bytes as binary level tiles; content surfaces only as corrupted level geometry/level-name string in the UI, so this is primarily a sandbox-boundary violation and crash primitive rather than a practical exfiltration channel.
findings.preconditions: Victim opens the crafted .rep via Load Replay; desktop mode. No network side exists to send the read bytes to.
findings.validation_plan: Craft evil.rep with '-1' as line 3 and '../../../../etc/hostname' (or Windows equivalent) as line 4, plus valid player lines; load it; console shows the resolved path being read (add breakpoint/log at ApoIO.java:216) and level geometry derived from that file's bytes, proving out-of-directory read.

findings.title: Plain-HTTP level transfer infrastructure inherited from framework, but unreachable in this variant
findings.code_excerpt: URL connectionURL = new URL(fileName); HttpURLConnection connection = (HttpURLConnection)connectionURL.openConnection(); connection.setDoOutput(true);
findings.entry_point: Theoretical: ApoIO.writeLevel/readLevel URL branches execute only when ApoConstants.B_APPLET is true (set solely by ApoMarioApplet's static block / ApoAppletBufferedStrategy); likewise ApoImage.getImage would fetch images via ImageIO.read(new URL(pic)) (ApoImage.java:92-93)
findings.sink: HTTP PUT/POST of level bytes to an arbitrary URL string (ApoIO.java:166-171) and cleartext URL image reads (ApoImage.java:93)
findings.data_path: In applet mode every caller is disabled: file choosers are never created (ApoMarioComponent.java:102-116), editor/replay/player-load functions are guarded by !ApoConstants.B_APPLET (e.g. ApoMarioMenu.java:403-408,421,454-462), and the only server constant APPLET_LEVEL="http://apo-games.de/apoMario/" (ApoMarioComponent.java:37) has zero references in the whole tree. So no live network path exists today; this documents dormant cloned infrastructure.
findings.attack_scenario: If a future variant re-enables applet-mode saving, level bytes (and any URLs handed to writeLevel) would travel unencrypted over HTTP, allowing a network MITM to read/inject level submissions. Today an attacker gains nothing: there is no reachable call site.
findings.preconditions: Would require resurrecting applet deployment (dead since browser applet support ended) or new callers passing bURL=true; none exist in this snapshot.
findings.validation_plan: Static proof: grep confirms single occurrence of APPLET_LEVEL (definition only) and that all writeLevel/readLevel(URL) invocations in apoMario.* go through overrides forcing local files; runtime proof: run ApoMarioApplet in appletviewer and verify no socket to apo-games.de is opened (tcpdump/lsof) because all IO buttons are hidden/disabled.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream/readObject anywhere in the 109-file tree (repo-wide grep)
weak_integrity_check - no MessageDigest/MD5/hash usage; this variant has no highscore submission or update-check logic to protect
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens or keys in source or constants
information_disclosure - no telemetry; only console stack traces (e.g. ApoIO.java:179,231)
legacy_sandbox_assumption - applet entry point exists but contains no doPrivileged/SecurityManager assumptions beyond the dormant HTTP code covered in ApoMario-05
notes: Source root contains a single tree, _from_jar_ApoMario/ (decompiled-from-jar layout), 109 .java files. This variant has NO highscore/level-server client (no save_highscore.php/save_level.php/get_level.php strings, unlike sibling variants) - the only server reference is the unreferenced APPLET_LEVEL constant. The real risk concentration is the AI-plugin model: ApoMarioClassLoader (game-specific, distinct from the dead shared org.apogames.help.ApoClassLoader, which is present but never instantiated here) executes arbitrary .class bytes with full privileges, and mario.properties (read from CWD, not user.home) auto-reloads the last AI paths at every startup, giving a persistence primitive. Other cloned-infra files present but unreferenced (dead code): org.apogames.help.ApoCopy, apoMario/level/ApoMarioLevelIO (its parser repeats the same unvalidated-dimension pattern as ApoMario-02 and would become finding-worthy if ever wired up). Quirk worth noting for clone-diff studies: hardcoded 'Team Icarus' easter egg burns any AI whose self-reported getTeamName() contains 'Team Icarus' near the level end (ApoMarioLevel.dieIcarus, ApoMarioLevel.java:1358-1374) - trivially spoofable client-side identity trust, cosmetic impact only since scoring is purely local. ApoMarioLevel.java imports test.IcarusAI and test.TestSolve whose sources are absent from this dump (jar-only classes). Malformed numeric fields in .rep headers additionally throw uncaught NumberFormatException (crash-on-open robustness issue folded into ApoMario-03).
